question: In applying Ampere-Maxwell law to a charging capacitor, one surface passes through the wire and another surface passes between the capacitor plates. What current term is present in each case? Explain.

options.A: A surface through the connecting wire has conduction current $I_C$ because charges cross it. A surface between the capacitor plates has no conduction current but has displacement current $I_D=\varepsilon_0\dfrac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ due to changing electric flux. For a charging capacitor, the two currents have the same value.
options.B: Both surfaces have only conduction current because charges cross the capacitor gap.
options.C: The surface through the wire has displacement current only, while the surface between the plates has conduction current only.
options.D: Both surfaces have no current term because the capacitor gap breaks the circuit.
